stories.angle: With the Series 3 draft at Parkway Bank Sports Complex tomorrow (Aug 22), all eyes shift to whether Romero (+42 in Series 2) or Lemley (+26) can build enough momentum in Series 3 to challenge Kowalik's lead before the individual champion is crowned after Series 4 on Aug 30. facebook.long_form:
Tomorrow is AUSL Series 3 draft day in Rosemont, Illinois — and the individual title race is officially in its final chapter.

Here's the situation heading into the draft at Parkway Bank Sports Complex:

Kowalik holds No. 1 in the individual standings. She's been dominant all summer. Romero surged +42 points in Series 2, climbing all the way to No. 9. Lemley added +26 more points. Both are closing — but Kowalik's lead hasn't disappeared.

With only Series 3 and Series 4 remaining, the math gets simple: Romero and Lemley need to perform at the highest level in both series, while hoping Kowalik stumbles. In a format where team wins generate individual points and individual statistical performances also count, there's no passive path to the title. You have to do the work in every game.

Tomorrow's draft is when Captains Ricketts, Coffey, and Netz make their picks — and every selection matters not just for team wins, but for the individual standings. This is what the AUSL All-Star Cup was designed for: layered, genuine competition where every decision has multiple meanings.

Series 3 tips off Sunday, Aug 24. The individual champion is crowned Aug 30 after Series 4.

Who are you watching in the final stretch? 🥎

stories.title: September 1 Countdown — 11 Days, Two-Phase Window
stories.angle: With 11 days until September 1, recruits should understand that Sept 1 is actually a two-phase opening. Sept 1 (communication) opens calls, texts, and emails from D1 coaches. Sept 9, 2026 at 7:00 AM ET is when the in-person contact window opens — the first time coaches can visit a recruit or a recruit can take an official visit. Families preparing only for Sept 1 calls could be caught off guard by the in-person timeline.

x_posts.label: Post 2
x_posts.text: 11 days to September 1. Two things Class of 2028 needs to know: Sept 1 = coaches can call and text for the first time. Sept 9 at 7 AM ET = in-person contact window opens (official + unofficial visits). Two deadlines. Prepare for both. #SoftballRecruiting 🥎

facebook.long_form:
11 days until September 1 — but here's what a lot of Class of 2028 families don't know: September 1 is actually just Phase 1.

Phase 1 — September 1:
D1 coaches can now call, text, and email recruits directly for the first time. The phones start ringing. Group chats light up. Coaches who have been watching film for months finally get to have a real conversation.

Phase 2 — September 9, 2026 at 7:00 AM ET:
The in-person contact window opens. This is when coaches can visit recruits at their homes, schools, or events. And recruits can take official visits to campuses for the first time.

If your family is preparing for September 1 but hasn't mapped out the September 9 timeline, you may be behind on scheduling. Official visit weekends fill fast — especially at top programs. Schools start reaching out about fall unofficial visits the moment coaches can contact you.

Recommendation for the next 11 days: Know your schools. Know your answer to "Can we schedule a visit?" Have your fall schedule accessible. Don't let the second wave catch you unprepared.

The 1,226 players who received EIS nominations this year — a record for the class — are all going through the same process. Preparation is what separates recruits who commit on their own terms from those who feel rushed.

11 days. Get ready for both phases. 🥎

article.headline: 11 Days to September 1: The Two-Phase Contact Window Class of 2028 Needs to Know

stories.angle: With 22 days until the WBSC Women's Softball World Cup Group Oklahoma opens, explaining what the format means: six teams (USA, Netherlands, Mexico, China, Brazil, New Zealand) compete in Devon Park, Oklahoma City. Top two advance to the 2027 Finals in Redcliffe, Queensland (near Brisbane, April 5–11) — the direct LA28 Olympic qualifier. USA is ranked No. 2 in the world. The stakes: a World Cup Finals berth, and with it, the path to LA28.

facebook.long_form:
22 days until Team USA opens the WBSC Women's Softball World Cup — Group Oklahoma — at Devon Park in Oklahoma City.

This is the event where USA punched its LA28 Olympic ticket. Or at least where they'll try.

Here's how it works: six teams play round-robin in Oklahoma City (Sept 12–16). The top two advance to the 2027 Finals in Redcliffe, Queensland, Australia — just outside Brisbane — on April 5–11, 2027. The Finals is where the official LA28 Olympic berths are awarded.

USA's group opponents: Netherlands (No. 6 in world), Mexico (No. 7), China (No. 8), Brazil, and New Zealand.

This is not a soft draw. The Netherlands and China have upset potential. A slip in group play is still possible.

But USA enters ranked No. 2 in the world, with a 16-player roster that includes four Oklahoma Sooners — Alyssa Brito, Jayda Coleman, Tiare Jennings, and Kelly Maxwell. Rachel Garcia and Dejah Mulipola are Olympic veterans anchoring the squad.

The road to LA28 goes through Devon Park this September. 22 days. ⏳ 🇺🇸

article.headline: 22 Days to OKC: USA Softball's Path to Brisbane Runs Through Group Oklahoma

facebook.long_form:
Patty Gasso's summer rebuild is entering its final phase — and the Sooners are making every move count.

The latest addition: Macie Harter, a transfer from Middle Tennessee State who hit .346 with 7 home runs and 23 RBI last season, earning Second Team All-Conference USA honors. She brings two years of eligibility and figures to compete for playing time immediately.

Combined with the 2027 recruiting class — Payton Westra (No. 2 overall, outfielder from Mesa, AZ) and Ori Mailo (No. 4 overall, No. 1 infielder from Waianae, HI, who enrolled early in 2026) — Gasso is building toward a genuine reload, not just a rebuild.

The losses hurt: Kasidi Pickering (.384 career at OU) is at Texas Tech. Tia Milloy is also gone. After Oklahoma's first WCWS miss since 2015, this offseason was always going to be aggressive.

The summer portal window is nearly closed. If Gasso has one more move to make, the clock is ticking.

Fall camp is coming. The 2027 Sooners are taking shape. 🥎

stories.title: Texas Softball — Three-Peat Context: Why History Is Against Them
stories.angle: Texas is going for its third straight WCWS title in 2027, which would make them only the third program in history to accomplish it. UCLA won three straight (1988–90), Oklahoma won three straight (2021–23). No other program has done it in the modern era. Teagan Kavan (2x WCWS MOP, first in history) returns to anchor the pitching staff. Fall camp is underway with 24 players and 11 new additions.

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: Only 2 programs have ever won 3 straight WCWS titles: UCLA (1988-90) and Oklahoma (2021-23). Texas won back-to-back in 2025-26. Teagan Kavan (2x MOP, first in history) is back. Fall camp underway. The Longhorns are chasing history. #HookEm #TexasSoftball

facebook.long_form:
Here's what makes a Texas three-peat in 2027 so rare — and so compelling.

Only two programs in the history of college softball have won three straight Women's College World Series titles:

UCLA — 1988, 1989, 1990.
Oklahoma — 2021, 2022, 2023.

That's it. In the entire modern era of D1 softball, only two programs have pulled it off. The competitive nature of the sport — the portal, the transfer rules, the talent distribution — makes sustaining dominance across three consecutive seasons extraordinarily difficult.

Texas won in 2025. Texas won again in 2026, going 49-12. Teagan Kavan became the first player in WCWS history to win the Most Outstanding Player award twice.

Now fall camp is underway. The Longhorns have 24 players on roster with 11 new additions, including a former Oklahoma pitcher via the transfer portal. Kavan is back as a senior.

If Texas wins in 2027, they would be the third program in history to accomplish the three-peat — joining UCLA and Oklahoma in a category that barely exists.

Are the Longhorns capable? Fall camp is where you find out. 🤘

article.headline: The Rarest Achievement in College Softball: Why a Texas Three-Peat Would Be Historic
